entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.4.3 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.4.3 Run two separate businesses on one computer. Each business keeps its own settings, saved passwords and keys, files, history and, if you choose, its own Claude account. The business name in the top bar switches between them, and switching closes the open office properly first. Add a business while the open one keeps working. Setup opens over the office, and the new business's folder is named after it. Back up everything and restore it on a new computer. One file holds every business, with saved passwords and keys locked by a backup password. Always allowed, for the privacy check. entries.title: v0.4.2
entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.4.2 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.4.2 Team members attach files from their folder. Ask a team member to email a client the statements in its folder, and the files go with the email. On Send on approval the card lists each file: open it, or take it off before you approve. A file a teammate keeps is handed over first. Slow shares no longer stall a turn, and a network path is never shown as missing. Quoted text in the terminal links the file inside it, when the quote is a sentence rather than a path. entries.title: v0.3.9
entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.3.9 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.3.9 Pulse can change a job's set times for you. For a job that runs at set times or on chosen days, Run less and Run more offer its own times thinned or filled in, ready to apply with Undo. No more stuck loading screen after sleep. A window left on the loading screen when the Mac wakes is noticed and loaded again. Links to files with spaces in their names open, in a tab, instead of showing the raw path. A job change that cannot work says why, instead of asking you to try again for something a retry cannot fix. entries.title: v0.3.8
entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.3.8 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.3.8 A lighter app. Features owners never used are gone: voice, webhooks, Slack, the History tab, languages other than English and every AI engine but Claude Code, Codex and Gemini. All clear has something to say. With every question answered, Michael offers one tip from your office, a saving or an unused connector, or shows what the team did today. Pulse shows each change you applied, on its own line, with what it saves or costs and its own Undo. More private. The prompts you type to team members are no longer saved, and the ones an older version saved are deleted. entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.3.7 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.3.7 Cards show what they rest on. The pages, records, emails and files behind an Ask me card sit as chips under its question, and a card that says nothing was found shows where the team looked. Focus on one department, with a row of chips on Ask me, and answer a question with a file: paste a screenshot, drop a file or use the paperclip. A job update is worked into the member's own job, and its card shows exactly which lines it adds, changes and removes. Each team member works within its role. It asks the teammates who could know before Michael, and records such as the customer list live with the role that keeps them. A safer office. What's new in 0.3.6 Anything your team finds for you reaches Needs you. Things only you can do wait on a card until you press Done, and notices with real stakes, such as money or a deadline, wait until you clear them. Routine email stays with the team. A question you leave open is never just dropped. The team member who asked decides whether to drop it, settle it or ask again, now or later. Open the original. A document links the file and email it came from, and an email attachment opens read only in its own app. Word documents keep their headings, lists and tables, and cards are short summaries that link their email. entries.title: v0.3.5
entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.3.5 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.3.5 Get featured: a case study of your office. Pulse builds a customer story page in your own brand, with how your office is set up and the hours the team worked while you were away. Every number comes from Pulse, and you send it to us from your own mailbox. A custom REST connection can hold a saved call. Team members send only their words; the fixed parts stay fixed. Foundation lists stay open until you say that's all, and what your team's work sees waits for you to decide. A first click on an email opens it, and a sleeping Mac no longer holds a team member back. entries.title: v0.3.4
entries.note: Don't Be Michael v0.3.4 An AI office for your small business. Pick your kind of business, pick your team, and Michael, your office manager, runs the floor while you run the business. What's new in 0.3.4 Give one team member access to one outside service. Custom integrations reach only the members you name, at Read only or Can change, and taking access away holds on the next call. Team members save email attachments. They go to the member's own folder, ready to read. Teammates hand files over by asking. The app carries the file across, so nobody opens another member's folder. Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files open in an office tab, and a card that names a folder opens that folder. The dock stays calm.
